arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argued Congress enacted the Class Action Fairness Act to protect absent class members.
the side that brought the case contended the stipulation binds the entire civil action filed by the representative.
the opposing side argued the text of the statute focuses on the specific claim amount.
the opposing side noted that absent class members can bring their own claims before certification.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Standard Fire Insurance Company seeks to remove a class action to federal court. the opposing side argues the claim does not meet the statutory threshold. The Court must interpret the Class Action Fairness Act of 2005.

paragraphs: This case defines the federal jurisdictional threshold for class actions. It determines which courts hear these disputes. It affects the balance of power between state and federal courts.
